parsed_result.rationale: Stack-trace summarization is centered in `src/query/stacktrace.rs`. It parses Python `File ... line ...` frames plus generic `path:line:col` shapes used by Rust, JavaScript/TypeScript, and Java-style traces, de-duplicates frames in first-seen order, normalizes paths, and resolves them to indexed files by path suffix with basename fallback for bare filenames. `src/cli/mod.rs` wires this into `agent-context --error <FILE>`: it reads the error log, calls `query::stacktrace::parse_stack_trace`, bypasses the daemon fast path for error-frame requests, then passes the parsed frames into context building. `src/query/mod.rs` applies those frames in `apply_error_context`, injecting or boosting matching files to an explicit `ERROR_TRACE_SCORE` of 5000, adding `why` text such as `appears in provided stack trace (line N)`, clearing test-offtopic penalties, and attaching the tightest indexed definition symbol covering the frame line when available. The resulting agent packet exposes the relevant source file, score, reason, symbols, snippets, call/reference context, related tests, and blast-radius fields through `ContextOutput` and `ContextFile`. The relevant index structures are in `src/store/mod.rs`, while `src/indexer/mod.rs` and `src/indexer/symbols.rs` explain how source files and symbol spans are populated so stack frames can resolve to source files and enclosing frames/functions. `src/query/ranker.rs` provides the scoring/debug component type used to label the stack-trace signal. Unit tests inside `src/query/stacktrace.rs` cover frame parsing and file matching; a test inside `src/query/mod.rs` confirms a traced crash file is promoted ahead of lexical matches and gets its enclosing symbol attached.
